MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Employment Type: Temporary Various

Requisition ID: CAM29662

A Place to Call Home. A Network That Builds Your Future.

Newcastle and its surrounds, Port Macquarie, and Tamworth offer more than excellent employment opportunities, they provide outstanding places to live. From the picturesque coastlines of Newcastle and Port Macquarie to the inviting rural character of Tamworth, each location delivers a balanced lifestyle that is both relaxed and active, supported by a strong sense of community. These settings are well-suited to individuals, couples, and families seeking both professional growth and quality of life.

You will be part of a highly connected network of hospitals that are collaborative, education-focused, and committed to excellence in patient care and trainee development. Our Emergency Departments are growing not only in size, but in scope, providing opportunities beyond clinical service, including:

Research

Point-of-care ultrasound

Trauma care

Dedicated education terms

Simulation training

We are proud of our strong culture of learning, mentorship, and professionalism. Our mission is to develop trainees into not only outstanding emergency physicians, but also compassionate, well-rounded individuals who feel deeply connected to the communities they serve.

Where you will be working 

You will work across our dynamic Emergency Medicine Network, which includes:

John Hunter Hospital

The Maitland Hospital

Calvary Mater Newcastle

Belmont District Hospital

Tamworth Rural Referral Hospital

Port Macquarie Base Hospital

This network provides a rich mix of metropolitan and rural experience, as well as access to diverse specialty terms for ACEM trainees at all stages.

John Hunter Hospital, one of the busiest Emergency Departments in Australia, offers a high acuity setting with a focus on trauma and retrieval medicine. If your training pathway requires tertiary experience only, this can be fully supported within the network at John Hunter Hospital.

What you'll be doing

The primary purpose of a Stage 1 Emergency Medicine Trainee is to provide high-quality medical care, under appropriate supervision, to undifferentiated patients presenting to the Emergency Department.

Trainees are expected to work within the scope of their clinical experience and training, contributing to patient care in a collaborative, multidisciplinary environment. Seeking senior support and input when required is a core part of safe, effective practice.

This position contributes to and supports progression through Stage 1 of the Australasian College for Emergency Medicine (ACEM) Training Program. Our Emergency Medicine Network is fully accredited for Stage 1 training by ACEM, offering a diverse and comprehensive experience that prepares trainees for career success.

We are proud of our educational outcomes, including excellent Primary and Fellowship Exam pass rates, Structured, high-quality ACEM curriculum delivery and exam preparation

Training Opportunities Across Our Network

Our trainees rotate through a rich mix of clinical placements, including:

Tertiary and metropolitan adult and paediatric Emergency Departments

Intensive Care Units

Anaesthetics

Qualifications and experience commensurate with the Essential Requirements for the role.

Demonstrated ability to work with appropriate independence, commensurate with a level of a Specialist Trainee, within a supervised complex clinical environment.

Demonstrated ability to work effectively as part of a multi-disciplinary team in the planning, delivery and coordination of patient care.

Demonstrated high level written and verbal communication skills and ability to communicate effectively and respectfully with patients, family members and others members of the health care team

Demonstrated good organisational and time management skills and ability to manage competing priorities in a complex environment.

Demonstrated commitment to quality improvement, patient safety and risk management.

Evidence of continuing professional development and commitment to self-education.

Previous experience in and willingness to deliver undergraduate and postgraduate medical education and training

About the role
Melbourne Automotive Engineering has been delivering trusted repairs, diagnostics, and tuning from our Bundoora workshop to Melbourne drivers and major insurers alike. With a scope that covers everything from routine servicing through to complete engine rebuilds, we are now looking for an experienced Mechanic to join our team. This is a hands-on trade role for someone who takes their work seriously and holds themselves to a high standard on every job, regardless of what comes through the door.

Key responsibilities
- Work across a steady mix of servicing and repair jobs, managing your own time and keeping jobs moving without sacrificing the standard of work
- Diagnose problems properly, using both hands-on knowledge and electronic diagnostic equipment to find the actual fault before touching anything
- Carry out repairs and mechanical rebuilds accurately, using manufacturer documentation as the benchmark and verifying your work before anything goes back to the customer
- Handle routine maintenance with the same attention as the bigger jobs, because preventative work done well keeps customers off the lift longer
- Assess vehicles for roadworthiness and prepare accurate reports or certificates where your qualifications allow

About you
- Trade-qualified mechanic (or with relevant experience) with genuine workshop experience and the diagnostic ability to back it up
- Someone who takes pride in their work and doesn't cut corners when rebuilding or reassembling
- Comfortable with computerised diagnostic tools and able to interpret what they're telling you
- Organised and self-directed, able to move between jobs without losing focus on quality
- Current driver's licence essential

Please note that this position is multi-classified as either an Administrative Services Officer Level 8 (ASO8), Allied Health Professional Level 4 (AHP4) or Registered Nurse-Midwife Level 4 (RN-M4). Appointment will be made at the appropriate classification based on the successful applicant's qualifications, registration and professional background.

About the Role

The Principal Service Design Manager provides strategic leadership to drive service design, transformation and continuous improvement across the Limestone Coast Local Health Network. Reporting to the Executive Director - Operations, this role will play a pivotal role in delivering the Limestone Coast Local Health Network's Clinical Services Plan, leading system-wide reform initiatives that improve service delivery, organisational performance and consumer outcomes. Working collaboratively with Executive leaders and key stakeholders, you will influence strategic decision-making and help shape the future delivery of health services across the region.

About You

You are an experienced strategic leader with a proven ability to influence organisational change, lead complex service redesign initiatives and work collaboratively across multidisciplinary environments. You bring exceptional leadership, stakeholder engagement and project management skills, together with the ability to provide high-level advice that shapes organisational strategy.

To succeed in the Principal Service Design Manager role, you will:

Demonstrate extensive experience leading strategic service redesign, transformation or organisational improvement initiatives.

Have highly developed leadership, stakeholder engagement and influencing skills within a complex organisation.

Possess proven experience managing large-scale programs or projects and delivering measurable outcomes.

Hold relevant tertiary qualifications and, where applicable, current professional registration appropriate to the appointed classification.

Demonstrate the ability to provide high-level strategic advice to executive leadership and contribute to organisational planning and reform.

About Operations

The Operations Directorate provides strategic leadership and operational oversight across the Limestone Coast Local Health Network, ensuring safe, effective and sustainable health services for our communities. The directorate works collaboratively across clinical and corporate portfolios to lead service planning, transformation, performance improvement and the delivery of strategic priorities that enhance healthcare outcomes across the region.

About the Limestone Coast Local Health Network

The Limestone Coast Local Health Network (LCLHN) delivers essential health services to more than 67,000 people across South Australia's south-east, while also supporting communities in Western Victoria. With over 1,800 staff and approximately 250 volunteers, LCLHN is a major regional employer committed to safe, high-quality, and community-focused care.

Our services extend from the Victorian border to the iconic Limestone Coast, delivering acute, community, and aged care services across a diverse network of sites. Working at LCLHN means being part of an organisation that plays a vital role in the health and wellbeing of its communities.

Beyond the work, LCLHN offers an exceptional lifestyle in one of Australia's most liveable regional destinations, where professional impact is matched with genuine work-life balance.

Why the Limestone Coast Local Health Network?

Make a meaningful difference as a trusted and valued part of the community.

Enjoy relaxed, affordable living with access to beaches, national parks and outdoor adventure.

Be part of a supportive, inclusive and collaborative team culture.

Access professional development, education and flexible working options.

Benefit from salary packaging and wellbeing initiatives.

Live midway between Adelaide and Melbourne, with the best of regional and city life.

Click the image above to learn more about a career with the Limestone Coast Local Health Network.

Conditions of Employment

A current Nationally Coordinated Criminal History Check (NCCHC) for employment involving unsupervised contact with vulnerable groups is required.

A current Working with Children Check (WWCC) is required.

For the AHP4 classification: Appointment is subject to meeting the LCLHN Credentialling requirements for Allied Health and Scientific Health Professionals.

Immunisation Risk for this position is Category B.

SA Health Services are required to implement the Addressing vaccine preventable disease: Occupational assessment, screening and vaccination policy 

Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion

The Limestone Coast Local Health Network is committed to building a flexible, diverse and inclusive culture, planning for and promoting diversity. We welcome and encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people as well as diverse community groups and ages including LGBTQIA+, people living with disability and other diversity groups. LCLHN recognises the benefits that such an approach brings for our staff and consumers in being an employer of choice.
